warnings: Afghanistan AIS publishes the current AIP, airspace NOTAMs and flight permission workflow. No reusable drone-zone geometry feed was verified; check current official publications and permissions before flight.

The Government of Andorra publishes drone FAQs and the 2025 UAS regulation, defining free, limited and prohibited flight zones. No current public zone map or reusable geometry download was verified; confirm the planned area and permissions with the authority.

Permit submission is through the MyGov service; check current AIP, NOTAMs and legal requirements before flight.
PANSA requires pilots to check current zones and notify intended flights through the DroneTower app. No documented anonymous reusable geozone feed was verified.
CAA Czechia designates DroneMap as the practical source for exact boundaries and operating conditions. No documented reusable public zone endpoint was verified.
The official page publishes a dated KML ZIP. Aeris can discover and inventory every placemark and style locally, but does not redistribute geometry while reuse terms remain unstated.
MyDroneSpace is Hungary's official pre-flight and operational service. No documented anonymous reusable national geozone feed was verified.
The Romanian CAA publishes prohibited/restricted UAS areas, contacts and an interactive map, but no stable reusable zone feed or reuse licence was verified.
The local inspection adapter discovers the newest BGR_ZONES package, but Aeris does not redistribute it while Bulgarian CAA reuse permission remains unconfirmed.
Check B-FLIP and active or temporary restrictions before flight.
HCAA requires a pre-flight DAGR check; yellow and magenta zones can require approval or prohibit flight. No documented reusable public feed was verified.
The public AMC map displays UAG, ULG and URG drone zones and current airspace. Registration is needed for operational reservations or approvals; no reusable public geometry feed was verified.

All approved Lithuanian geozones and temporary restrictions are published in the UTM platform. Its user rules apply to registered users; no documented public reusable feed was verified.

DCA publishes regulations and an authority handoff; no public drone geofence or reusable zone geometry was verified. Check current DCA requirements, AIP and NOTAMs before flight.

Offline packages include open airport-with-air-navigation-services points, WGS84 5.6 km orientation rings, and national-park boundaries. This is not a complete certified aerodrome/heliport or controlled-airspace map.
NRC states its NAV CANADA-derived airspace geometry cannot be redistributed. Use the official Drone Site Selection Tool for exact controlled airspace and current restrictions.
CASA directs pilots to verified apps. Its digital platform data access is for onboarded providers and authenticated services, so Aeris does not bypass that access model.
CAA directs pilots to AirShare for current low-flying, aerodrome, control, restricted, military and danger areas. No documented reusable public feed was verified.
DIPS 2.0 is the official registration, planning and permission platform. No documented anonymous reusable national zone feed was verified.
SARPAS requires operator and aircraft registration for access requests. Aeris does not automate or bypass the authenticated operational service.
Digital Sky is the government real-time repository for red, yellow and green airspace zones. No documented anonymous public API or reusable zone download was verified.
CAAS identifies OneMap as the authoritative source for no-fly, permit and temporary restricted areas. No documented reusable UA-zone feed was verified.
The authoritative restrictions are published through current AIP/NOTAM and SACAA RPAS rules. No national public drone-geozone feed with reuse terms was verified.

GCAA’s official interactive map shows no-fly and prohibited zones. The KMZ link on its registration page returned 404 during review; this registry links to the functioning map and does not claim a reusable downloadable feed.
ANAC publishes national AIP charts and restricted, prohibited and dangerous area information. Current amendments and NOTAMs must be checked; no reusable drone-zone feed was verified.
SENEAM publishes official aeronautical charts and airspace restrictions; AFAC directs RPAS operators to AIP restrictions. No reusable national drone-zone feed was verified.
CAAC identifies UOM as the national unmanned-aircraft management and airspace service. Local governments publish detailed controlled-airspace extents; no reusable public national feed was verified.
SHGM’s official İHA system displays green free-flight areas and manages permissions. Check local flight bans and current AIP/NOTAM restrictions.
CAAT identifies this as its official drone operations service. Check the current airspace restrictions and temporary notices in the portal.
CAAP provides an official coordinate lookup for critical areas. It requires a CAPTCHA and agreement, so Aeris links pilots to the authority instead of automating the lookup.
AirNav Indonesia publishes AIP, aeronautical charts and NOTAM. Drone permissions are managed through Ministry of Transport SIDOPI-GO; check both sources.
CAAM UAS guidance identifies airspace classes and restrictions; the current AIP contains official airspace maps. No reusable drone-zone feed was verified.
Aerocivil states the public UAS geographic viewer displays drone no-fly zones and RAC 100/AIP restrictions. No data reuse terms were verified.
The Ministry of National Defence publishes nationwide prohibited and restricted UAV areas in its public map portal. No reusable feed or redistribution terms were verified.
GACA regulations require pilots to consult its published UAS geographical zones; the official portal manages registration and permits. No public reusable zone feed was verified.
Transport Malta publishes the national geographical-zone overview and links its interactive map from this official page. No reusable public zone feed or redistribution permission was verified.

The official Air Navigation (Overseas Territories) Order contains Anguilla UAS rules and requires ATC permission in specified controlled airspace and aerodrome traffic zones. No reusable current drone-zone geometry was verified; check AIP/NOTAMs and permissions directly.

The BHANSA AMC map visibly includes an RPAS/UAS layer and warns that its preview does not replace current NAUP/NUUP and NOTAM checks. BHDCA publishes national drone rules including border-protection limits and airport/CTR coordination requirements. No reusable zone geometry or redistribution licence was verified.

ACAA directs operators to AIP-defined prohibited or restricted zones; Albcontrol publishes an effective digital AIP with official airspace charts. No reusable public drone-zone geometry was verified; check current AIP amendments and NOTAMs directly.

The current Armenian eAIP requires advance applications to the Civil Aviation Committee for RPAS training and special flights and publishes airspace charts. No reusable drone-zone geometry was verified; check current AIP, NOTAMs and permissions.

ANAC SIAD publishes aeronautical information and ICAO charts; NTA 36 contains RPAS approval rules. No current public drone-zone map or reusable geospatial feed was verified. Check the current AIP, NOTAMs and ANAC permissions.

The public map provides indexed ASPA/ASMA/HSM locations but not precise georeferenced boundaries. The updated 2024 AAD polygon download requires an email request; no contact information was submitted. Verify management plans and expedition permissions directly.
